CLASS SB AS "System.Text.StringBuilder". 01 O USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE SB. Rule: A.1 103) 'I-O status (action taken for fatal exception conditions). This item is required. This item shall be documented' -> §9.1.13.1 'If the value of the I-O status for an input-output operation indicates a fatal exception condition, the implementor determines what action is taken ... The implementor may either continue or terminate the execution of the run unit.' CONFORMANCE.md: NO '| DOC-A.1-103 |' row; the only statement of the action is a parenthetical inside the SORT/MERGE implicit-transfer bullet of §3 ('if the implementor continues the run unit (COBOL.NET does, with checking off)'), plus §2 row 44 'Nonzero process exit on an unresumed fatal exception condition'. Code fixes a two-arm determination (probes at pin): checking OFF (default) -> execution CONTINUES after a fatal status even with no FILE STATUS and no USE (f2: OPEN INPUT absent non-optional file = '35', READ = '47', both continue, exit 0; f6: line-sequential WRITE of X"01" = '71' continues, exit 0); checking ON (>>TURN EC-I-O / EC-ALL CHECKING ON) -> 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR (fatal): I-O status 35', exit 1. 9x is defined fatal (IsFatalIoStatus). DIVERGES (silent): the determination is made in code but not registered, and the in-code documentation CONTRADICTS the default arm: FileStatus.cs LineRecordInvalidChar's summary says 'a program without a FILE STATUS item or a USE declarative terminates here rather than writing a corrupt line' — measured false in a default build (f6 continues, exit 0). Related open note kb/Work/PB1512 (host IOException on READ/WRITE escapes as an unhandled .NET crash instead of '30' + the item-103 action) — referenced, not re-reported; no note owns the documentation half -> new finding. Editions: §9.1.13.1 is not listed in Annex E as changed. cite.py --check 9.1.13.1 'The implementor may either continue or terminate the execution of the run unit' -> OK §9.1.13.1 (General).

Rule: A.1 111) 'LEAP-SECOND directive (whether a value greater than 59 seconds may be reported and, if so, the maximum number of seconds that may be reported). This item is required. (ACCEPT GR11, CURRENT-DATE r1, WHEN-COMPILED r1). CONFORMANCE.md: no '| DOC-A.1-111 |' row. The determination IS written, but MISNUMBERED: the §3 directives bullet says '>>LEAP-SECOND (§7.3.17) — the REPORTED side only: the .NET clock never reports a 60th second (A.1 item 112)' — item 112 is the >= 86,400 standard-numeric-time item (its own §7 row exists); the seconds-position question is item 111. Behaviour matches the prose by reading: every reported time derives from System.DateTime (AcceptSource.Time = Hour*1000000 + Minute*10000 + Second*100 + ms/10, DateTime.Second is 0..59), so no seconds value > 59 is ever reported under ON or OFF. PARTIAL: substance present, not registered under item 111, filed under the wrong item number, and no test pins the reported side (not forceable on a host clock). Referenced, not re-reported. Rule: A.1 113) 'Life cycle for objects (timing and algorithm for taking part in continued execution). This item is required. This item need not be documented in the implementor's user documentation.' -> §9.3.14.3 'An instance object is destroyed either when it is determined that the object cannot take part in the continued execution of the run unit, or when the run unit terminates, whichever occurs first. The timing and algorithm for the mechanism that determines whether or not an instance object can take part in the continued execution of the run unit is implementor-defined.' Documentation not required (audit register documented=False), so the absent §7 row is correct. Behaviour: a COBOL object is a managed .NET instance deriving CobolObject; reachability is decided by the .NET tracing garbage collector (the NOTE's 'garbage collection'), timing nondeterministic as the rule permits; the only object-owned resource with observable destruction (a per-object instance file, §9.1.4) is closed by a re-armed finalizer on collection, with CobolFile.CloseAll() at run-unit termination as the 'whichever occurs first' backstop. Probe at pin: conformance golden 2002/oo_object_file_two_instances re-run, output identical. Empty test-ref: no spec-derived test pins collection timing (it is implementor-defined and nondeterministic, so no test can). No owning note. cite.py --check 9.3.14.3 'The timing and algorithm for the mechanism that determines whether or not an instance object can take part in the continued execution of the run unit is implementor-defined' -> OK §9.3.14.3. || REFUTER OVERTURN (CONFORMS -> PARTIAL): Doc: A.1 item 113 need not be documented (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:34452). cite.py: 'OK §9.3.14.3 (Life cycle for instance objects) The timing and algorithm ... is implementor-defined.'; 'OK §9.1.4 (Open mode) — For file connectors in an object when the object is deleted.' The adjudicator's mechanism ('per-object instance files are closed by a re-armed finalizer') is DEAD CODE. ~CobolObject (src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Control/CobolObject.cs) calls CobolFile.EnqueueInstanceClose → `_reg => RunUnit.Current.Files` (CobolFile.cs:17), and RunUnit.Current is `_current.Value ??= new RunUnit()` over an AsyncLocal (RunUnit.cs). The GC finalizer thread does not carry the mutator's ExecutionContext, so it MINTS AN ORPHAN RunUnit and enqueues there; FileRegistry.DrainPendingObjectCloses on the real run unit never sees the key. Proof harness /tmp/adj/refute/h/P.cs (references the built Cobol.Net.Runtime.dll; subclass calls __TrackInstanceFile, GC.Collect+WaitForPendingFinalizers): output 'finalizer-thread ambient: a DIFFERENT (orphan) RunUnit; orphan pending=1' / 'main-run-unit pending closes after GC = 0'. COBOL-observable: /tmp/adj/refute/gc2.cob (--std 2002): loop {NEW WCLS; method W does OPEN OUTPUT of its instance file gc.dat + WRITE (no CLOSE); SET A TO NULL; 1,500,000 throwaway NEW JCLS} → 'K=00000002 OPEN-OUTPUT=61' — the second object's OPEN is refused as a sharing conflict by the first, unreachable object's connector, and stays refused forever. /tmp/adj/refute/gc1.cob: after dropping the writer and ~4M allocations, main OPEN INPUT of gc.dat → READ=10 (the record 'AAA' never flushed; the connector was never closed). So an object the runtime HAS determined cannot take part (its finalizer ran) is never destroyed as COBOL observes destruction (§9.1.4's implicit CLOSE 'when the object is deleted') until run-unit end, and FileRegistry keeps every minted per-object connector (and its OS handle) alive for the life of the run unit — unbounded growth for programs creating file-owning objects. §9.3.14.3 sentence 1 requires destruction 'when it is determined'; the §9.1.4 NOTE licenses GC delay, not a close that can never happen. Run-unit-end CloseAll still closes them (the 'whichever occurs first' backstop holds), and file-less objects are reclaimed correctly by the GC — hence PARTIAL, not DIVERGES. Tests: test-ref empty; golden 2002/oo_object_file_two_instances only covers explicitly CLOSEd/live objects and cannot see this. No kb/Work note found for the orphan-RunUnit finalizer (grep 'AsyncLocal|orphan|finalizer' over kb/Work) — needs a new defect note (areas runtime/oo + runtime/io; sibling sweep: any other finalizer/threadpool callback reaching RunUnit.Current). Static registries otherwise checked: CobolSort.Files, PointerImage.s_nameBases, collation caches hold no object references; PointerImage.s_areaBases is a ConditionalWeakTable. || code-location commentary (registrar-normalized, kb/Work PB1522): src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Control/CobolObject.cs#CobolObject (GC.SuppressFinalize / __TrackInstanceFile / finalizer) | .NET garbage collector | src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Control/RunUnit.cs#Current (AsyncLocal)

Operative text §12.4.5.10.3 GR2: 'Each record in a line sequential file is terminated by an implementor-defined line delimiter' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.10.3 -> OK §12.4.5.10.3 2); NB the Annex's '12.4.5.10' alone FAILS --check, the rule sits in the General rules subclause .3). CONFORMANCE.md: NO '| DOC-A.1-114 |' row. The only mention is off-key inside DOC-A.1-115 (the character-set row): 'the two line delimiters CR U+000D and LF U+000A' - which names the characters excluded from the set but does not state the delimiter a WRITE emits nor the READ-side recognition rule. Code fixes both halves: OpenWriter builds the write handle with NewLine = "
" (every WRITE ends the record with CR LF); ReadPhysicalLine accepts LF, lone CR, or CR LF as the terminator, and a final line with no terminator ends at EOF. Probes: ls1.cob (--std 2023) writes 'AB' and 'CDE' -> od shows 'A B

CC' with PIC X(5) -> [AAAAA] 06, [AAA  ] 00, [BB   ] 00, [CC   ] 00, then 10 - so lone CR, lone LF and EOF all delimit and the §9.1.13.2 '06' arm fires on the over-length line. The behaviour is settled and plausible, but the required documentation under its own key is absent -> DIVERGES (harm silent). Rule: A.1 item 116 'Linkage section (whether access to linkage section items is meaningful when called from a non-COBOL program). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon support for calling a COBOL program from a non-COBOL program. This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented... (13.7, Linkage section)' (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 116)). Operative text §13.7.4 GR3: 'If a program is activated by a non-COBOL runtime element, the implementor defines whether access to formal parameters and the returning item is guaranteed' (cite.py --check 13.7.4 "the implementor defines whether access to formal parameters and the returning item is guaranteed" -> OK §13.7.4 3)); GR5's non-COBOL-activator sentence (initial value of linkage items) is its twin. The CONDITION HOLDS: CONFORMANCE.md §3's 'Return to a NON-COBOL activating runtime element' bullet (kb/Work PB408) declares a .NET host activating a generated program to be a supported non-COBOL activator, and the public entry ProgramRegistry.CallProgram(name, callerPath, CobolArg[] args, CobolArg? returning, ...) maps a host's CobolArg[] positionally onto the LINKAGE formals exactly as ICobolProgram.Call does for a COBOL caller, while ICobolProgram.Activate leaves linkage UNBOUND (ProgramEmitter's UNBOUND seed, §13.7.4 GR3). So a determination exists in code (access guaranteed when the host passes args through CallProgram; unbound under Activate) but CONFORMANCE.md has NO '| DOC-A.1-116 |' row and the §3 bullet says nothing about linkage access -> DIVERGES (harm silent). Not re-reported: owning note kb/Work PB1253 (open, 'linkage-section' finding: 'Write DOC-A.1-116 ... item 116 also needs the behaviour DECIDED for ICobolProgram.Call/Activate entered without a COBOL caller'). Umbrella kb/Work A11. No spec-derived test drives a non-COBOL activator. Editions: LINKAGE SECTION and the non-COBOL-activator rule exist in every edition; the host ABI is edition-independent.

General rule 1' lives in subclause .3). §6.5 'The implementor shall define the effect on the source listing, if any, of logical conversion.' (cite.py --check 6.5 -> OK §6.5 9)). Code: COBOL.NET produces NO source listing - the CLI (cobol --help) has no listing option and no listing writer exists in src; >>LISTING is recognized and held as NONE HELD in DirectiveStateRegistry citing §7.3.18.3 GR1; probe lst.cob (>>LISTING OFF / >>PAGE / >>LISTING ON, --std 2023) compiles clean and prints HI. So 'whether' = never, 'when' = never, and the logical-conversion effect is vacuous - a coherent determination. Rule: A.1 item 118 'Locale specification (how user and system defaults defined; at least one user and one system default). This item is required. This item need not be documented in the implementor's user documentation. The implementor may specify that the user locale and the system locale are the same locale. (8.2, Locales)' (cite.py --check A.1 -> OK §A.1 118)). §8.2.1: 'The implementor shall specify the manner in which the user default locale is defined and shall provide at least one user default locale for use in computing environments that do not provide a user default locale' and the SYSTEM twin (both cite.py --check 8.2.1 -> OK §8.2.1). No documentation obligation, so part (a) is waived (there is no '| DOC-A.1-118 |' row; the manner IS nevertheless written voluntarily: CONFORMANCE.md §4 A.4.9 locale paragraph 'the user default from COBOL_USER_LOCALE (else the process culture, else the root)', RuntimeConfig.All's COBOL_USER_LOCALE / COBOL_SYSTEM_LOCALE entries, DESIGN-locale-facility §4.3 table, DETERMINATION L2 = owner decision Q2). Part (b), the behaviour: LocaleState() sets UserDefault = Determine(COBOL_USER_LOCALE, CultureInfo.CurrentCulture) and SystemDefault = Determine(COBOL_SYSTEM_LOCALE, CultureInfo.InstalledUICulture); Determine returns the env value, else the culture name, else '' (the root) when the host has no culture data - so at least one user and one system default ALWAYS exist, including environments that supply none. SystemDefault has no setter (§8.2.1 'The capability of setting the system default locale from COBOL is not provided'). Probe loc.cob (--std 2023; SET LOCALE LC_ALL TO SYSTEM-DEFAULT / USER-DEFAULT then FUNCTION LOCALE-DATE): env COBOL_USER_LOCALE=de-DE COBOL_SYSTEM_LOCALE=fr-FR -> SYS 24/09/2026, USR 24.09.2026 (two distinct defaults, each honoured); env unset + DOTNET_SYSTEM_GLOBALIZATION_INVARIANT=1 -> both 09/24/2026, no exception, rc 0 (the root fallback). Tests: the unit test SetFromSystemDefault asserts CurrentLocale == SystemDefault; pb64t1_set_locale_categories runs SYSDEF/USERDEF arms under the harness's pinned INVARIANT defaults. Caveat for the refuter: no test pins the unset-env culture fallback arm (it is host-dependent by design); verified by probe only. Editions: the locale facility (A.4.9) is 2002+. Owning note: none (grep item 118: none); design owner kb/Work PB64 (landed T1).
